Sarah / Mina — brief TL;DR from infra side after digging:
- At 08:45 PT an automated routing policy change (internal rollout) increased the small-batch lane share for a new partner test, which reduced available slots for AtlasHealth's prefetched KV keys.
- The reduced concurrency + bursty priority for certain prefixes caused a hot-key eviction cascade: repeated repopulation attempts and prefetch storms.
- HOL (head-of-line) blocking observed where long KV fetches were stalling batch formation, increasing queueing delay.
- We also saw a transient kernel-level scheduling pressure on the NVLink path on nodes serving your group (we're checking if colocation contributed).

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Rolled back the routing change at 09:08 PT (rollback diff attached: route_config_diff_20270315.patch).
2) Temporarily pinned AtlasHealth routes to a reserved lane with dedicated small-batch capacity to avoid inter-tenant interference.
3) Increased KV cache TTL in-region for the most-frequently-accessed prefixes for 30m to reduce repopulation.

Metrics so far: p99 is trending down from 2.2s -> 650ms; 503s back to ~0.6%. We're still monitoring for stability and will keep you posted.

- Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah/Kevin — thank you again for the patience while we stabilized your traffic. Attached is the summary we discussed in the exec briefing and the short-term remediation we have scheduled. Key points: 

1) Root cause (short): an automated routing lane redistribution was rolled out to increase small-batch throughput for a partner test. The change unintentionally reduced effective concurrency for AtlasHealth's pinned prefixes, triggering frequent KV evictions and repopulation storms. The repeated cache misses combined with long tail KV fetches caused HOL blocking and queue saturation on the small-batch lane.

2) What we did (short-term):
- Rolled back the routing redistribution (09:08 PT).
- Temporarily reserved 30% of small-batch lane capacity for AtlasHealth until policy-level controls are in place.
- Increased TTLs and enabled per-prefix prefetch backoff for the next 2 hours to dissipate repopulation spikes.
- Deployed a hotkey mitigation that routes high-frequency prefixes to a pinned in-memory store for critical routes.

3) Metrics (post-mitigation):
- p99: 2.2s -> 420–700ms (stabilizing near ~450ms under load).
- 503 rate: 3.6% -> 0.3% over the 3h window.
- Throughput: returned to baseline within ~22 minutes of rollback.

4) Next actions (medium-term, owners & ETA):
- Rishi: per-tenant reservation feature (GA guardrail & UI) — ETA 3 weeks.
- Vivek: prefetch backoff policy improvements + auto-throttle when eviction rate > X — ETA 2 weeks.
- Mina/CS: SOW addendum to include tighter SLAs for critical routes and credit proposal for outage impact — ETA 4 business days.

5) Compensation & customer communication:
- We propose a one-time service credit of 5% of this month’s committed spend while we complete the medium-term mitigations. Laura will draft the official offer.
